```{r scratch-viz-setup, include=FALSE}
# Publication figure system: house theme, validated colour-vision-safe palette,
# and vector (PDF) output alongside every raster figure. Applied globally, so
# the plotting code below needs no changes. Guarded: if the library is not
# staged, the notebook renders exactly as it did before.
local({
  roots <- c(".", "assets/viz", Sys.getenv("SCRATCH_VIZ_DIR", "."))
  for (lib in c("scratch_viz.R", "scratch_report.R")) {
    for (r in roots) {
      p <- file.path(r, lib)
      if (file.exists(p)) { source(p, local = FALSE); break }
    }
  }
})
```

## Loading Seurat object

```{r LoadingDta}

# Reading seurat object
seurat_object <- readRDS(file = seurat_object)

# Reading reference object
reference_object <- readRDS(file = reference_object)

# Ensure reference has a 'seurat_annotation' column
meta_cols <- colnames(reference_object@meta.data)

if (!"seurat_annotation" %in% meta_cols) {
  if ("seurat_annotations" %in% meta_cols) {
    # create an alias so downstream code works unchanged
    reference_object$seurat_annotation <- reference_object$seurat_annotations
  } else {
    stop(
      "Reference object has no 'seurat_annotation' or 'seurat_annotations' column. ",
      "Available metadata columns are: ",
      paste(meta_cols, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }
}



# Setting random seed
random_seed <- 2203
set.seed(random_seed)

```
## Projecting annotation

```{r Anchors}
#| output: false

# find anchors
anchors <- FindTransferAnchors(reference = reference_object, query = seurat_object)

# transfer labels
# TransferData defaults to k.weight = 50, but a small or poorly-overlapping
# reference can yield fewer anchors than that and the call dies with
# "Please set k.weight to be smaller than the number of anchors". Scale k.weight
# to the anchors actually found instead of hard-failing the whole stage.
.n_anchors <- tryCatch(nrow(slot(anchors, "anchors")), error = function(e) NA_integer_)
.kw <- if (is.na(.n_anchors)) 50L else max(2L, min(50L, .n_anchors - 5L))
if (!is.na(.n_anchors) && .n_anchors < 30)
  warning(sprintf(paste("Only %d transfer anchors were found between query and reference;",
                        "using k.weight = %d. Label transfer on this few anchors is weak --",
                        "treat the Azimuth labels as provisional and check the prediction",
                        "scores before relying on them."), .n_anchors, .kw), call. = FALSE)

predictions <- TransferData(
  anchorset = anchors,
  refdata = reference_object$seurat_annotations,
  k.weight = .kw
)

```

## Adding metadata

```{r RenamingAnnotation}

# Renaming annotation column
predictions <- predictions %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    azimuth_labels = predicted.id
  )

# Adding labels
seurat_object <- AddMetaData(
```

```{r CellDimPlot}
#| label: fig-azimuth-celldimplot-split
#| fig-cap: "Azimuth UMAP — click a cell type on the right to hide it, double-click to show it on its own"
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8

# Was one static panel per label: 11 near-identical grey UMAPs with a few
# coloured dots each, most of the ink spent redrawing the same background, and
# the small populations (Mast, 11 cells) invisible at that size. A single
# interactive UMAP does the same job better -- plotly makes each cell type its
# own trace, so the legend IS the selector: click to drop a population,
# double-click to isolate it.
#
# Built with plain ggplot rather than SCP::CellDimPlot on purpose. The shim only
# promotes point-ONLY plots to the large-scatter path, and CellDimPlot adds label
# and stat layers that disqualify it, so it would have stayed a static raster.
.emb <- as.data.frame(Seurat::Embeddings(seurat_object, "umap"))[, 1:2]
names(.emb) <- c("umap_1", "umap_2")
.emb$label <- as.character(seurat_object@meta.data[["azimuth_labels"]])
.emb <- .emb[!is.na(.emb$label), ]

# Order the legend by population size, so the eye meets the big populations
# first instead of an alphabetical list.
.counts <- sort(table(.emb$label), decreasing = TRUE)
.emb$label <- factor(.emb$label, levels = names(.counts))
.emb$tip <- sprintf("%s\n%s cells (%.1f%% of cohort)",
                    .emb$label,
                    format(as.integer(.counts[as.character(.emb$label)]), big.mark = ","),
                    100 * as.numeric(.counts[as.character(.emb$label)]) / nrow(.emb))

ggplot(.emb, aes(umap_1, umap_2, colour = label, text = tip)) +
  geom_point(size = .25, alpha = .85) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(title = "Azimuth cell-type annotation",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s cells, %d labels; legend doubles as a filter",
                          format(nrow(.emb), big.mark = ","), length(.counts)),
       x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2", colour = NULL) +
  theme_scratch()
```

## Azimuth dendrogram

```{r annotation_tree}
#| warning: false

# Aggregate data by annotations
cell_average <- AverageExpression(
  seurat_v4, 
  assay = 'RNA',
  layer = 'scale.data',
  return.seurat = FALSE, 
  group.by = "azimuth_labels"
  )

cell_average <- cell_average$RNA

# Compute distance matrix on aggregated data
cell_dist_matrix <- as.matrix(cell_average)
cell_dist_matrix <- stats::cor(cell_dist_matrix, method = "pearson")

# Convert correlation matrix to a distance matrix
cell_dist_matrix <- stats::as.dist(1 - cell_dist_matrix)

# Perform hierarchical clustering
cell_hierarchical <- stats::hclust(cell_dist_matrix)

```

```{r dendrogram-finding, results = 'asis'}
#| warning: false
# Computed at render time from the same hclust the figure draws, so the text can
# never drift from the tree beside it.
if (exists("cell_hierarchical") && length(cell_hierarchical$height)) {
  .m <- cell_hierarchical$merge; .h <- cell_hierarchical$height
  .lab <- cell_hierarchical$labels
  # The first merge is by definition the closest pair; it is only interpretable
  # when BOTH sides are leaves (a leaf-to-cluster join is not a pair of labels).
  .leafpairs <- which(.m[, 1] < 0 & .m[, 2] < 0)
  .cnt <- table(as.character(seurat_object@meta.data[["azimuth_labels"]]))
  if (length(.leafpairs)) {
    i <- .leafpairs[which.min(.h[.leafpairs])]
    a <- .lab[-.m[i, 1]]; b <- .lab[-.m[i, 2]]
    n_ab <- sum(.cnt[c(a, b)], na.rm = TRUE)
    msg <- sprintf(paste(
      "**%s and %s are the least separable pair of labels here** -- they join at a",
      "height of **%.2f** (Pearson r = %.2f between their mean expression profiles),",
      "the earliest merge of any two labels in this tree. **%s cells** carry one of",
      "those two labels, so if the boundary between them is wrong, that is how many",
      "cells move. Treat any result that depends on separating these two -- composition",
      "shifts, differential abundance, cell-cell communication -- as the weakest claim",
      "in the report, and check it survives merging them into one class."),
      a, b, .h[i], 1 - .h[i], format(n_ab, big.mark = ","))
    scratch_finding(msg, type = if (.h[i] < 0.5) "caution" else "note",
                    title = "Least distinct annotations")
  }
}
```

```{r figDendrogram}
# `text` is not a ggplot aesthetic -- ggplotly consumes it for the hover label --
# so a static build warns "Ignoring unknown aesthetics: text".
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: 'Dendrogram'
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-align: center

# Base graphics could not be made to appear here: the previous version drew the
# tree correctly to figures/FigDendogram.png but emitted NOTHING inline, leaving
# the literal words "NULL" and "png 2" in the report where the figure should be.
# Rebuilt as a ggplot from the hclust segments, so it is the chunk's VALUE and
# goes through the same knit_print -> interactive + auto-export path as every
# other figure. Horizontal layout so long cell-type names have room to sit
# without overlapping, which the vertical base-R version could not manage.
.dend_gg <- function(hc) {
  n     <- length(hc$order)
  # x = leaf position in plotting order, y = merge height.
  xpos  <- numeric(nrow(hc$merge)); ypos <- hc$height
  leafx <- match(seq_len(n), hc$order)
  getx  <- function(k) if (k < 0) leafx[-k] else xpos[k]
  gety  <- function(k) if (k < 0) 0          else ypos[k]
  segs  <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(hc$merge))) {
    l <- hc$merge[i, 1]; r <- hc$merge[i, 2]
    lx <- getx(l); rx <- getx(r); ly <- gety(l); ry <- gety(r)
    xpos[i] <- (lx + rx) / 2
    segs[[length(segs) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      x = c(lx, rx, lx), xend = c(lx, rx, rx),
      y = c(ly, ry, ypos[i]), yend = c(ypos[i], ypos[i], ypos[i]))
  }
  list(segments = do.call(rbind, segs),
       leaves   = data.frame(x = seq_len(n), label = hc$labels[hc$order]))
}

.dd <- .dend_gg(cell_hierarchical)

# A bare tree says "these branches are near each other" and stops there. What a
# reader actually needs is which labels are hardest to tell apart, and how many
# cells ride on that. Leaf size = population, hover = counts, and the finding
# below names the closest pair explicitly.
.ncells <- table(as.character(seurat_object@meta.data[["azimuth_labels"]]))
.dd$leaves$n <- as.integer(.ncells[.dd$leaves$label])
.dd$leaves$n[is.na(.dd$leaves$n)] <- 0L
.dd$leaves$pct <- 100 * .dd$leaves$n / max(1, sum(.dd$leaves$n))

ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = .dd$segments,
               aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
               linewidth = .45, colour = "#31506b", lineend = "round") +
  geom_point(data = .dd$leaves,
             aes(x = x, y = 0, size = n,
                 text = sprintf("%s\n%s cells (%.1f%% of cohort)",
                                label, format(n, big.mark = ","), pct)),
             colour = "#0d366b", alpha = .85) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 9, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = .dd$leaves$x, labels = .dd$leaves$label,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(.05, .05))) +
  scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = c(.12, .02))) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "How distinct are the annotated cell types?",
       subtitle = paste("branches join at 1 - Pearson r between mean scale.data profiles;",
                        "an EARLY join = two labels the data barely separates.",
                        "\nPoint area = number of cells carrying that label"),
       x = NULL, y = "height (1 - Pearson correlation)") +
  theme_scratch() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

```

```{r FindAllMarkers}
message(">>> [DE] running FindAllMarkers for azimuth_labels at: ", Sys.time())

seurat_annotation <- seurat_v4
Idents(seurat_annotation) <- "azimuth_labels"

all_markers_azimuth <- tryCatch(
{
FindAllMarkers(
object = seurat_annotation,
assay = "RNA",
only.pos = FALSE,
test.use = "wilcox",
logfc.threshold = 0.25,
min.pct = 0.1
)
},
error = function(e) {
message(">>> [DE] FindAllMarkers ERROR: ", conditionMessage(e))
return(NULL)
}
)

if (is.null(all_markers_azimuth)) {
message(">>> [DE] FindAllMarkers returned NULL; downstream DE plots will be skipped.")
} else {
message(">>> [DE] Total markers (azimuth_labels): ", nrow(all_markers_azimuth))



saveRDS(
all_markers_azimuth,
file = file.path("data", paste0(project_name, "_DE_azimuth_all.rds"))
)

DE_azimuth_sig <- subset(
all_markers_azimuth,
avg_log2FC > 1 & p_val_adj < 0.05
)
message(">>> [DE] Significant markers (log2FC > 1 & padj < 0.05): ", nrow(DE_azimuth_sig))

saveRDS(
DE_azimuth_sig,
file = file.path("data", paste0(project_name, "_DE_azimuth_sig.rds"))
)
}
```

```{r fig-azimuth-de-heatmap}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-cap: "Azimuth DE heatmap (top markers per label)"
# Enlarged to the size the removed duplicate used -- at 14x10 the gene names
# were unreadable. `dev: pdf` dropped: it made this the only raster-less figure
# in the report and it rendered smaller than everything around it.
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-path: "figures/azimuth_de_heatmap_"

if (exists("DE_azimuth_sig") &&
    is.data.frame(DE_azimuth_sig) &&
    nrow(DE_azimuth_sig) > 0 &&
    exists("top_markers_heat") &&
    nrow(top_markers_heat) > 0) {

  p_heat <- DoHeatmap(
    object  = seurat_annotation,
    features = unique(top_markers_heat$gene),
    group.by = "azimuth_labels",
    # `size` is the group-label text along the top. At the default 5.5 with 45
    # degrees, the narrow groups (Mast = 11 cells, NK, pDC, Endothelial) had
    # their labels printed on top of one another. Smaller and vertical: 90
    # degrees costs height, which this figure has, instead of width, which the
    # narrow groups do not.
    size  = 3.2,
    angle = 90
  ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "B") +
    theme(
      # DoHeatmap's x axis is one tick PER CELL. Drawing 24,000 rotated barcode
      # labels produced the solid grey band under the plot -- not small text, a
      # wall of overlapping text carrying no information. The coloured group bar
      # along the top already says which cells belong to which label.
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      # ~60 gene names down the side: 7pt still collided, 5.5 fits.
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 5.5)
    ) +
    labs(x = sprintf("cells, grouped by Azimuth label (n = %s)",
                     format(ncol(seurat_annotation), big.mark = ",")))

  p_heat
} else {
  plot.new()
  text(0.5, 0.5, "No significant DE markers available for heatmap.")
}

```
